Boxing and kickboxing, for someone who wants to get fit and for someone who wants a fight.
A coach will set the work to where you are, and to what you came for.
Showers, changing rooms, and gloves you can borrow
Classes for where you are, and for what you want.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: shadow boxing or pad work.
Stance first, then pads, then sparring when you are ready.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: kicks on the pads.
Hands, kicks, and knees. A full workout, and a useful way to leave the day behind.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: women training and enjoying it.
The athletic part of the sport, without being thrown into sparring. A good class if you are new, and a class a lot of women use.
Coaching that holds up in a fight
The coaches have been in fights, and they teach what they actually use.
You are not put in to spar on day one. You build up to it.
Getting in shape, or getting a bout. We help you keep showing up for whichever one you chose.
Clothes you can move in, and indoor shoes
Wraps and gloves, which you can borrow
Don't train straight after a meal
Tell us about an injury or a condition before you train
You can come and watch first
Questions people ask before they join.
I've never really trained. Is that a problem?
No. Most people here started that way.
No. Sparring is for people who ask for it, and only once they're ready.
Yes. There is also a women-only class. Replace this if you don't have one.
Can I train toward a fight?
Talk to a coach. The work can be built around that.
You can come and watch. No need to train on the first visit.
